title: There is no eligible official-price set in the committed Season 2 run
detail: The development sandbox's direct urllib request to Nasdaq ended with a TLS EOF, although the official endpoint was retrievable through the page-fetch path. A GitHub Actions adapter now supports collection and preserves raw bytes, but Nasdaq's public-site legal terms do not establish permission to redistribute the response in this repository. The existing Yahoo files remain reproducible SECONDARY research data, not eligible official prices; the strict Season 2 command refuses to trade until the audit passes.
fix: Run the official collector on GitHub Actions, obtain a documented redistribution/licensing status for the official source, review the raw/checksum/coverage report, then rerun the official-price gate and Season 2. Never replace the Yahoo files silently.

title: The committed Season 2 price files are secondary, not official
detail: The historical Season 2 memory uses Yahoo daily OHLCV, dividends and splits. Those are real observations but Yahoo is an aggregator and every file is marked SECONDARY. The official Nasdaq adapter is separate and the eligibility gate checks all 24 tradable symbols; no current Season 2 result is promoted merely because two publishers agree.
fix: Collect and license the official-source candidate, pass sim.eligibility, then run Season 2 against the named official backend. The engine already carries per-fill file, checksum, date, reference close, volume, participation, spread, impact and fee fields.

title: Decisions happen once per session; a decision can be *worked* at the open or the close, never mid-session
detail: A participant writes one order list per session. Since IR-34 each order can carry at_close, which works it against the venue's final interval instead of the first, so a market-on-close exit and an overnight-only entry are now expressible and are what GapAndGo and OvernightCarry use. What is still not expressible is any mid-session reaction: no strategy can see a print at interval 5 and act on it, so a stop that in real life would trigger at noon is modelled as triggering at the next scheduled decision. Intraday scalping, vwap-following and reaction-to-news strategies remain out of reach, and any result quoted for a strategy whose edge is claimed to be intra-hour should be read as a coarse approximation of it.
fix: Closed for the part that was a venue limitation rather than a data one: Order.at_close plus engine routing (IR-34). The mid-session reaction limitation is a daily-bar replay limitation and needs the minute-bar engine in REMAINING_WORK.

title: Each participant trades an independent replica of the venue
detail: Impact and dealer inventory are per-participant, so one competitor's flow never changes another's fills. That makes the leaderboard independent of processing order and every run exactly reproducible, but it means the participants' combined flow does not clear a single shared book - in a real market, twenty aggressive participants trading the same names would move the price for each other.
fix: A shared venue with a deterministic clearing step per interval, or an aggregate-flow impact term added to the replica mid. Either changes reproducibility guarantees and needs its own test suite.

title: No corporate-event data of any kind
detail: There is no earnings calendar, no EPS surprise series, no short interest, no days-to-cover, no float, no news, no analyst revisions, no index reconstitution, no stock splits and no corporate actions beyond the declared cash dividends. Two strategies are forced onto price/volume proxies as a result (IR-07), and no participant can react to an event that is not in the price already.
fix: Vendor event data. The cheapest high-value additions are an earnings-date calendar and FINRA short-interest files; both are published and machine-readable.

title: Cash earns nothing and debit balances are financed only through declared borrow fees
detail: Risk-free rate is zero throughout: Sharpe and Sortino are computed against zero, cash balances earn no interest, and margin debit balances are not charged a broker financing rate. Over a year at realistic 2025-2026 rates that is a material omission for levered participants, and it flatters every strategy that runs a cash deficit. It is also why the ratios are internally consistent - mixing a real T-bill rate into the numerator while paying no carry on cash would make them meaningless.
fix: Add a financing curve (SOFR or T-bill plus a declared spread) to CostConfig, accrue it daily in Account.accrue_carry, and subtract it in the Sharpe numerator. Roughly a day of work once the rate source is chosen.

title: Participants are strategies, not people
detail: The competitions this project reverse-engineered track human traders who register, log in and click. StockPaperSim tracks Python classes with usernames. There is no authentication, no account creation, no order-entry UI and no self-registration, so the site is a results archive rather than a contest platform.
fix: A web front end with auth, an order ticket that posts to a broker API backed by this engine, and per-user account state. The engine's per-participant venue replica design already supports adding participants at runtime.

title: One competition year is one observation
detail: No ranking produced from a single 251-session path is statistically significant. A participant that finishes first may simply have held the name that drew well; the diagnostics showed exactly this mechanism at work (IR-19). The six-scenario robustness panel is a partial mitigation, not a substitute for many independent years, because all six share the same real index path.
fix: More scenarios with independently drawn market factors, longer archives of real data, and formal significance testing (bootstrap confidence intervals on Sharpe and alpha; Deflated Sharpe Ratio after Bailey and Lopez de Prado) before any result is described as skill.

title: The declared priors decide a large part of the outcome
detail: Beta, idiosyncratic volatility, declared alpha, ADV, borrow availability and borrow fees per instrument are design inputs chosen to span a realistic cross-section. They are not vendor statistics and not forecasts. A strategy's rank is conditional on them: with different alphas, a different participant wins.
fix: Publish the priors next to the results (the data-provenance page does exactly this, field by field), and re-run the season against priors estimated from real historical data once L-01 is resolved.

title: Market microstructure is a stylised single-venue model
detail: There is no venue fragmentation, no dark pools, no order routing, no market-on-close auction, no real queue-position tracking (resting limit fills use an approximate fill-ratio from how far the path traded through the limit), no iceberg detection, and one blended maker/taker rate instead of per-venue fee schedules. Displayed depth is a stylised ladder rather than observed Level II data.
fix: Observed quote and depth data plus per-venue fee schedules; a queue-position model calibrated against real fill rates for resting orders; an explicit closing-auction mechanism.

title: Margin is a simplified Reg T plus a house maintenance rule
detail: Initial margin 50% per Reg T, a 2.0x gross cap and a 30% maintenance requirement are SIM CHOICES - The Leap allows only 1:1 on stocks. There is no special memorandum account, no house-call sequencing, no portfolio margin, and the pattern-day-trader rule is counted and reported but not enforced (these are paper accounts with no real broker behind them).
fix: An SMA-based equity computation with house-call sequencing, and PDT enforcement that restricts a participant to closing transactions for five sessions after the fourth day trade in a rolling five-day window below $25,000.

title: Two fee inputs rest on secondary sources or uncertain effective dates
detail: The FINRA Trade Activity Fee rate is now supported by FINRA's primary fee-adjustment schedule (IR-05). The SEC's 2024 half-penny tick tier and $0.001 access-fee cap remain subject to the documented temporary relief and future compliance dates (IR-04). Both are regulatory facts that remain pinned to primary sources, not broker summaries.
fix: Retrieve FINRA Schedule A and the current compliance-date order for the 2024 Reg NMS amendments, then pin both constants to the primary text.

title: The site is static and does not update itself
detail: docs/ is generated by scripts/build_site.py from run memory and published as-is. Nothing refreshes on a schedule, there is no live leaderboard feed and no intraday snapshot - unlike the referenced competitions, whose leaderboards update as often as hourly.
fix: A scheduled GitHub Actions job that re-runs the season and republishes, or a small API service serving the memory store with the site fetching it client-side.

title: Memory is compressed JSON Lines, not a database
detail: Queries are streaming scans over gzip files. At the published scale (36,597 event rows across 8 streams, 4.08 MB for the six scenarios) that is instant and has the advantage of being human-readable, dependency-free and trivially checksummable. It would not survive 10 million rows or concurrent writers.
fix: A SQLite or DuckDB backend behind the same MemoryStore interface; the JSONL files stay as the export format. The query API is already written against an iterator abstraction, so the swap is local.

title: No strategy can be added without editing Python
detail: The roster is a list of classes in sim/strategies.py. Adding a participant means writing code, which rules out the thing a competition platform exists for: letting people bring their own ideas.
fix: A declarative strategy format (JSON or a small DSL) interpreted by the engine, with the existing classes as reference implementations, plus validation that a submitted strategy cannot see future data.

title: Dividends are paid without a matching ex-date price drop
detail: Real price series gap down on the ex-date; the simulated series do not. For non-anchored names the generator compensates by removing the declared window dividend yield from the price drift, so total return is not double counted, but the day-to-day price path does not show the ex-date step that a real chart would. AAPL is exempt because its anchor is a real unadjusted close that already contains the real drops.
fix: Partly reversed: rather than force the price path to drop, the venue now charges the short side the dividend it owes (IR-31), so total return is consistent for long and short books whichever convention the price path follows. A real ex-date drop on simulated names is still not modelled, which is why the adjustment item stays in REMAINING_WORK: the two mechanisms must not both be applied without checking that the yield is not being charged twice.

title: Season 2 has one price history and no second one to compare against
detail: Season 1 could re-run the season under several idiosyncratic draws and report how ranks moved. Season 2 trades the real history, so its result is a single observation: a participant that finished first would not necessarily finish first again, and nothing in this repository can measure that. A real answer needs either a longer sample (several years of real prices, each run as its own season) or an explicit bootstrap of the real return path, and neither is in place.
fix: Run the same roster over several non-overlapping real years (the collector can already fetch a multi-year window) and publish the cross-year rank correlation, alongside the existing venue-stress panel.

title: Signal mapping from MasterSite projects to instruments is a judgement, not a measurement
detail: The MasterFeed register labels each mapping STRONG, WEAK or UNPROVEN, but the label is this project's reasoning, not an estimated relationship. Nothing here regresses sportsbook equity returns on MLB game counts, or biotech ETF returns on FDA approval counts. A strategy can therefore be well implemented and still be trading a link that does not exist.
fix: Estimate each mapping openly: regress the candidate instrument's returns on the signal with lags, publish the coefficients and t-statistics with the same file-level provenance as the prices, and let a WEAK mapping be reported as a measured zero rather than an asserted one.

title: Four of the twelve requested sources cannot be backtested from official records
detail: The NFL injury report, the NBA injury report, SportsPred's pre-game probabilities and (as archived history) the NCAA scoreboard are published live. Four participants are therefore forward-only: they are registered, their adapters point at the official documents, and they placed no backdated trades. Their 0.00% is an absence of evidence, not evidence of no edge.
fix: Let the collector run on a schedule so the live documents start accumulating a real, dated archive; after a season of daily collection those participants can be backtested on their own collected history with the same ledger.

title: Injuries and suspensions are only visible through price, not through position limits that vary by name
detail: The venue model applies one margin and borrow model to every name. Real desks face name-specific borrow availability, hard-to-borrow lists and recall risk, which is exactly the risk an injury-driven sportsbook strategy would face if it shorted a squeezed name. The Season 2 roster shorts DKNG, FLUT and PENN, so this is a live gap rather than a theoretical one.
fix: Add a per-name borrow-availability series (FINRA's daily short-sale volume and the OTC transparency data are the public starting points) and let a short fail to open when the name is on the hard-to-borrow list.

title: The published ledger is a summary of what the engine decided, not an independent execution path
detail: Every fill carries the real bar it filled against and is re-derived by an outside script, but both the fill and the reference come from the same run. If the venue model is wrong - the spread too tight, the impact exponent too small - the ledger will faithfully record a wrong price relationship, and no amount of hashing will catch it.
fix: Replay a sample of days against a real intraday print history (a single name, a handful of days) and compare the modelled fill price with the actual traded price at that minute; publish the error distribution as a calibration table rather than an assumption.

title: Season 2's signal coverage is what could be collected, not what the brief listed
detail: Fourteen projects were reviewed and five participants are idle: three wait on the Form 4 stream, one on a venue payload whose numbers are empty, one is a declared forward-only probe. Two further families that circulate widely (opening-range breakout, social-sentiment trading) are not implemented at all because they need intraday bars and platform data this project cannot collect. The register states each of these one by one, but the aggregate effect on the season is real: a third of the roster contributes no return information.
fix: Re-collect the missing sources (REMAINING_WORK P1/P2), and if the intraday feeds cannot be reached, say so on the site's front page rather than only in the register.

title: The live book's executable prices are secondary
detail: Signals, the benchmark, the calendar and the financing rate in the Live Book are official and free; the prices its fills execute against are the collected Yahoo research files marked SECONDARY. The book therefore reports official-price coverage of filled notional as a number - 0.00% in the current rehearsal - and cannot be an official-price competition until an eligible official security-price archive exists.
fix: Collect a licensed, redistributable official price set (REMAINING_WORK P0) and re-run the same live book over it; the code path does not change, only the reference files and their source class.

title: One decision point per session
detail: The live book decides once per session, after the close, and executes at the next session's open or close. Rules that need the shape of the session itself - the opening range, the first-hour volume profile, a stop that would have been hit intraday - cannot be expressed, and the roster says so instead of approximating them: @ORB_NextOpen_Probe is a declared forward-only probe with no intents.
fix: Expose several decision points per session on top of the intraday path (REMAINING_WORK P1).

title: Index histories are signals and benchmarks, never tradable legs
detail: The Nasdaq Composite, Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and VIX histories are official and free, and none of them is a security that can be bought. Every index rule therefore executes through an ETF proxy (QQQ, SPY, TLT), so tracking difference, fund fees and the proxy's own liquidity sit between the signal and the P&L. A reader must not read an index rule's result as the return of the index.
fix: Keep the proxy disclosed per participant (done on every live participant page) and, if futures access ever exists, test the same rules on the contract instead.

title: The forward book has no settled trades yet
detail: The real forward state of the live book is 16 pending intents planned on 2026-09-16 and aimed at 2026-09-17. Nothing has settled, no cash has moved, and the book correctly reports no return. The only measurable result today is the walk-forward rehearsal over already-collected sessions, which is a different (and weaker) claim than a live track record.
fix: Settle the pending book as soon as a verified bar for a target session exists, which needs either a licensed feed or the collection workflow running on a schedule.

title: The SEC insider extracts are not yet collected (HTTP 403 from the runner)
detail: The official lane's insider strategies and the MasterSite insider signal both need the SEC's quarterly Form 3/4/5 structured extracts. On the collection run of 2026-09-18 the runner was answered HTTP 403 at both documented path layouts for every quarter requested (eight quarters x two layouts), and data/real/insider_bulk/ is empty. Every attempt is recorded with its status in data/real/collection_manifest.json, so this is evidence rather than silence, but it means no insider rule can trade on official insider data yet.
fix: Correct the request (SEC's published bot headers, a longer back-off, or a different egress), or fetch the same extracts by hand from a network SEC accepts and commit them with the same SHA-256 ledger the other files carry.

title: The official book's secondary leg is derived, not published
detail: No free, redistribution-permitted publisher prints a secondary market trade tape for US Treasuries. The venue prices a secondary order from the Treasury's official par yield curve or from the H.15 bill discount rates by a formula printed on the venue page, and labels those fills OFFICIAL-DERIVED rather than OFFICIAL. The price is a function of a published observation, not a published transaction, and on the published run about 61% of closed-trade notional is in that class.
fix: Acquire a licence for a secondary trade tape (BrokerTec, Tradeweb, or the FRBNY's Treasury market data products) or replace the derived leg with a published benchmark whose terms permit redistribution.

title: TIPS are marked as clean real prices: no indexation is modelled
detail: An inflation-protected security's cash flows depend on the daily reference CPI index ratio applied to principal and coupon. The official lane discounts a TIPS at the official H.15 real yield for its tenor, which gives a clean real price, and does not collect the reference index series, so it understates the inflation accrual of a TIPS position held over the season. Every TIPS mark carries an 'indexation' note saying exactly this.
fix: Collect the Treasury's daily reference CPI and index ratios for the traded CUSIPs and carry the accrued inflation into the coupon and cash flows, or restrict the lane to nominal securities and label the TIPS rule as a research-only variant.

title: Auction awards are booked on the auction date with same-day cash
detail: A non-competitive award is priced at the auction, and the security is delivered and paid for on the published issue date, typically two to five business days later. The venue books the fill and the cash on the auction date so that every trade has one date, which is a declared simplification: it flatters a strategy that would have to fund the purchase between the two dates, and the declared financing terms are applied to whatever cash balance results.
fix: Split the fill into a trade date and a settlement date, charge the repo between them, and re-run the season to publish the difference.

title: The venue's maintenance rule is a house rule, not a regulation
detail: The book closes a position when equity falls below 5% of gross exposure and winds an account up at zero equity. Real margin on Treasury positions is set by the counterparty and varies with tenor, collateral and clearing arrangements (Reg T initial margin, NYSE Rule 431 maintenance, and cleared-repo haircuts all differ), so the 5% rule is this venue's declaration rather than a citation. It is stated in the manifest, printed on the venue page, and applied identically to every participant.
fix: Adopt a per-security haircut schedule with a published source for each row, then re-run and report how much of the difference in survivorship it explains.

title: Secondary liquidity is assumed, not measured
detail: Primary fills carry the auction's own liquidity statistics (offering amount, total accepted, competitive tendered, bid-to-cover) and the book records the request as a percentage of each. Secondary fills in an issued security execute at the derived price for any size the leverage cap allows, because no free publisher reports Treasury secondary depth. A very large secondary order therefore pays no spread and leaves no footprint, which is the same weakness the equity books record as L-23.
fix: Record a secondary-size limit per CUSIP from a licensed depth source, or cap secondary fills at a multiple of the auction's own non-competitive accepted amount and re-run.

title: The unified trade ledger mixes price classes; its totals are not additive
detail: The ledger normalises every closed trade from every book into one store so the same record can be re-used for analysis. The four books do not trade on the same kind of price: OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL-DERIVED rows rest on a government publisher's number, MODELLED rows are simulated paths, and SECONDARY rows are an aggregator's bars. Adding P&L across classes would produce a number with no meaning, so every published view of the ledger is split by class and the site prints the split beside the total.
fix: Keep the classes but add a per-class benchmark line, so a reader can see whether a class's aggregate P&L is explained by its own market rather than by the mix.

title: The official lane's sessions are the yield curve's business days
detail: The book's session calendar is the set of dates the official par yield curve covers. The Treasury publishes that curve on business days, including days when the securities market is closed (for example a federal holiday that is not a market holiday, or the reverse). A session on which a secondary order could not really have traded therefore appears in the tape, and no such session is filtered out.
fix: Intersect the curve's dates with the published market calendar the equity books already carry, and re-run the season on the intersection.

title: Insider strategies and the MasterSite insider signal remain unbacked
detail: The brief asks for insider-trade signals from the MasterSite review. The signal is defined and the strategy is on the roster, but with the SEC extracts refused (L-27) there is no official insider transaction data in the repository, so any participant trading that signal would be trading on nothing. The rule therefore plans no orders and the participant page says why, rather than substituting a secondary aggregator for an official filing.
fix: Resolve L-27, then run the insider rules over the collected quarters and publish their trade tapes alongside the others.

title: The inflation rule's realised leg is a lagged monthly observation, and before the 1990-window collection it did not exist at all
detail: The TIPS breakeven rule compares the breakeven at a security's remaining maturity with realised CPI inflation over the same number of years. Until 2026-09-19 the repository held one year of the index (data/real/fred/CPIAUCSL_2024-09-16_2026-09-17.csv, 25 observations), so on all 250 sessions the rule recorded that the series was too short for the thirty-year security it was looking at and stood aside - its published +5.58% at that point was interest on cash, and the site said so. The collector now asks for the index from 1990 (FRED_SERIES_WINDOWS in scripts/collect_real_data.py) and the loader picks the longest collected window; the wider file (440 observations, 1990-01-01 to 2026-08-01) landed in the next collection run and the rule traded. What remains is inherent to the measure: the inflation leg is a lagged monthly observation - the newest available at the session, about six weeks behind it - and it is *realised* inflation, not the inflation the market expects over the security's life, so even a correct comparison is a statement about the past rather than a forecast.
fix: Nothing further is required for the rule to compute its horizon. A rule that wanted the market's expectation instead of realised history would need a second official source (the Treasury's own TIPS-derived forward inflation rates, or a survey published by the Federal Reserve), which is not collected here and would be a new source rather than a repair of this one.

title: A bid on an auction that has not priced yet is sized from the newest published price of the same term
detail: A non-competitive bid is an order for a face amount, and the book turns a dollar target into face at a price. When the auction has not happened yet the Treasury has published no price for it, so the venue uses the newest published price for the same security type and term (par if the book has never seen that term) and records that in the bid's rationale. Only the face amount depends on that estimate: the cash the account pays is this auction's own published price, read at settlement, and the leverage check is re-run against it. The residual risk is that a large move in the days before an auction changes how much face the target implies, which moves position size slightly away from the declared dollar target.
fix: Nothing to correct in the price path; the item is registered because a reader comparing a strategy's declared dollar target with its settled face should know which price converted one into the other. If the lane ever collects a Treasury announcement its own price expectation, the sizing price should be that instead.
